question: GQ-001
subject: "irreducible" was another unmeasured word
what_i_wrote_last_turn: gates-are-load-bearing.sh is "~300s... irreducible for what it measures"
the_word_irreducible: I used it about the self-test one turn before finding a 6.5x speedup. It deserved the same scrutiny and did not get it.

but_57s_was_wrong_for_a_worse_reason.arithmetic_that_did_not_add_up: one chain run is 61s; nine runs should be ~549s, yet the suite finished in 58s
but_57s_was_wrong_for_a_worse_reason.cause: audit-verify-chain.mjs joined the chain as the FIRST gate this session. It reports chain-names-missing-gate for any gate named in package.json but absent from disk — so EVERY removal was caught by the guard, in 0s, before the gate under test ever ran.
but_57s_was_wrong_for_a_worse_reason.what_the_suite_was_really_reporting: "7 load-bearing" while testing one thing seven times
but_57s_was_wrong_for_a_worse_reason.this_is_the_defect_the_suite_exists_to_f: a pass for the wrong reason

fix.what: exclude audit-verify-chain.mjs from the chain under test
fix.also: each SKIP now states its own reason — the chain-guard was being labelled "reads git history", which is true of evaluate-refresh and false of it

the_pattern: Twice in two turns I published a timing I had not re-measured after changing the thing it timed. A number carried forward is an assertion, not a measurement.
